passage: Jomon, you're going to be a prefect, so let Seema Miss tell you about one boy from my years as a teacher. His name was Tenzin, and he had been making fake posts about a girl called Shruti. When it came out, the school suspended him for a week. But I also sat with him. I asked, "What did you get from this?" He said his friends only noticed him when he was being mean. We found him a counsellor, and he helped with the school magazine after that. He wrote Shruti a real apology. Shruti had counselling too, and she joined the debate club again. And the whole class had to talk honestly about who had watched and done nothing.

qa.a: He was suspended for a week.

qa.q: Why did Tenzin say he made the posts?
qa.a: He said his friends only noticed him when he was being mean, which suggests he wanted attention and belonging.

qa.q: What can Jomon learn from Seema Miss about repair?
qa.a: Real repair has several parts: a clear consequence for the boy, help for what drives him, support for the target, and a class that faces its own silence.

qa.q: How might Shruti feel as she rejoins the debate club?
qa.a: She may feel nervous but more confident, knowing the school took her side and she had support.

grounding: It shows a boy facing consequences and support to understand harm, the target regaining confidence, and bystanders learning silence costs something.

passage: The school hall's fans had broken in the heat, and the class meeting had only twenty minutes before the next period. The boy who had been posting cruel comments about Deepika had already been dealt with by the school, and he was seeing the counsellor every week. Now it was the class's turn. The teacher asked, "How many of you saw the posts?" Almost every hand went up. "How many said anything?" Two hands. Farida was one of them. The silence felt heavy. Deepika sat by the window, beside Farida, her head up this time. After weeks of sessions with the counsellor, she had started drawing again. When the bell rang, three classmates walked over to Deepika and said sorry for staying quiet.

qa.q: How many hands went up when the teacher asked who said anything?
qa.a: Two hands went up, and Farida was one of them.

qa.q: What does Deepika sitting with her head up suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she is feeling more confident and safe again after weeks of counselling and support.

qa.q: Why was the class meeting an important part of repair?
qa.a: It helped the whole class see that staying silent allowed the harm, which led three classmates to apologise and may make them act sooner next time.

qa.q: How might the classmates who stayed silent feel after the meeting?
qa.a: They likely feel uncomfortable and a bit guilty, realising their silence had a cost for Deepika.

grounding: It illustrates the bully facing consequences with support, the target regaining confidence, and the bystanders learning that silence has a cost.
